audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Yasuo four stages and Zac none, including both item brackets, on a lane the mirror rebalanced to Yasuo 3 / Skill 2 / Zac 2.
audit.why: The mirror (zac__yasuo) set win[2] and win[3] to Skill and win[5] and win[6] to Zac. Zac scales into a tank whose Unstable Matter is maximum-health damage and whose Cell Division revives him — a crit Yasuo does not simply keep beating him past two items.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 5 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as one atomic group with ratings, and every prose field that claimed the item brackets for Yasuo (whys[5], whys[6], spikes[2], late, phases[5].why, phases[6].why) rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text contained literal editorial debris — "Elastic Slingshot (R... his E)" — and no stage carried a cooldown.
audit.why: Stretching Strikes is 14/12.5/11/9.5/8s, Elastic Slingshot 21/18/15/12/9s, Unstable Matter a 5s cooldown, Let's Bounce! 120/105/90s. The 21s leap is the punish window the page kept gesturing at without naming.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text and spikes[2].text rewritten with the real numbers and the debris removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline advice — Wind Wall blocks Elastic Slingshot — is wrong, and it appears in the tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].t, report[5].t, whys[3], whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid and wants.you[2]. Riot's text for Elastic Slingshot is "attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward" — a leap, not a projectile. Wind Wall destroys projectiles.
audit.why: The mirror verified this as the matchup-inverting error, and the kit's derived projectile flag on E contradicts Riot's own description, so the description wins. Stretching Strikes IS the projectile and IS wallable — the page conflated the two. Also unstated: Elastic Slingshot carries a grounding effect, which is precisely what shuts your Sweeping Blade off after he lands.
audit.corrected: Every Wind Wall-blocks-the-leap claim rewritten to name Stretching Strikes as the wallable ability and the leap as something to side-step; the grounding written into dontsFull[1].d; Cell Division's blob healing and Unstable Matter's max-health damage written into dosFull[2].d, phases[5].why and spikes[2].text.
sources: enemyKit Q/E flags vs Riot text

notes: Highest-value correction here matches the mirror's: Wind Wall does NOT block Elastic Slingshot. Riot's text calls it a launch and the derived projectile flag contradicts the description, so the description was trusted — the page had told the reader to spend a 25-second cooldown on it in eleven places. Stretching Strikes is the projectile and stays wallable. Rows 2/5/6 proposed as one atomic paired group per the mirror, with every prose field that claimed the item brackets rewritten so the page does not argue with its own chart.
